cards.title: Log-log amortized decrease-key in standard pairing heaps
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(C>0\) such that the standard two-pass pairing heap defined below satisfies \[W(\mathcal S)\le C\left(a(\mathcal S)+b(\mathcal S)\log_2(N+2)+c(\mathcal S)\log_2\log_2(N+4)\right)\] for every finite legal operation sequence \(\mathcal S\) starting from empty heaps and having at most \(N\ge1\) live items in total? Here \(a\) counts make-heap, insert, meld and find-min operations, \(b\) counts delete-min, and \(c\) counts decrease-key. The fixed algorithm and work measure \(W\) are defined below.

cards.title: Erdős girth conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer \(k\ge 1\), do there exist constants \(c_{k}>0\) and \(N_{k}\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge N_{k}\), some simple undirected graph G on exactly n vertices has at least \(c_{k} n^{1+1/k}\) edges and contains no cycle of length less than \(2k+2\)? Equivalently, is \(M_{2k+2}(n)=\Omega _{k}(n^{1+1/k})\) for every fixed k, where \(M_{s}(n)\) is the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph with no cycle shorter than s?

cards.title: Excluded-grid treewidth exponent
cards.formal: Determine the excluded-grid exponent \(x_{\mathrm{grid}}\) to absolute error at most \(1/100\). For each integer \(r\ge2\), let \[f(r)=\min\{t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:\forall G,\ \operatorname{tw}(G)\ge t\Longrightarrow Q_r\text{ is a minor of }G\},\] where \(G\) ranges over finite simple undirected graphs and \(Q_r\) is the \(r\)-by-\(r\) square grid. Define \[x_{\mathrm{grid}}=\inf\{a\ge0:f(r)=O(r^a)\}.\] The precise asymptotic quantifiers, treewidth and ordinary graph-minor model are given below. The parameter \(r\) is grid side length, not its \(r^2\) vertices. Logarithmic factors are outside the requested precision.

cards.title: Near-linear-time exact Euclidean minimum spanning trees
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(d\ge3\), is there one deterministic algorithm \(A_d\), a constant \(C_d>0\), and an integer \(a_d\ge1\) that compute an exact Euclidean minimum spanning tree of any \(n\ge2\) distinct points in \(\mathbb R^d\) in at most \[C_d n\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^{a_d}\] worst-case steps in the real-arithmetic model below? The input is an array of coordinates \(p_1,\ldots,p_n\). The output is a list of \(n-1\) index pairs forming a connected acyclic graph \(T\) minimizing \(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in T}\|p_i-p_j\|_2\). The program and constants may depend on fixed \(d\), but not on \(n\) or the coordinates.

cards.title: Factor-two subtour-LP gap for asymmetric TSP
cards.formal: Is \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(c)\le2\,\mathrm{LP}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(c)\) for every integer \(n\ge2\) and every nonnegative directed metric \(c\) on \(n\) vertices with \(\mathrm{LP}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(c)>0\), using the Hamiltonian-tour objective and degree-constrained subtour linear program below? Equivalently, is the universal integrality gap \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{ATSP}}=2\), since the matching lower bound is known? This is an existence inequality; no efficient rounding algorithm is required.
